topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text: The neon's fading, the place where I'd lay down my hat, or at least a soggy fedora after too many nights of chasing shadows. Word on the street is, they're pulling the plug, shutting the doors. Might've been just a rumor, a ghost dancing in the rain, but no, the bartender, my usual stool, confirmed it. End of an era, just like the last time I believed something would stay put. I've got a bottle somewhere, half-empty, waiting for the right moment. Guess this is it. Not much left to say, except maybe, I'll miss the old flicker of light in the corner, the soft hum of a place that felt a little too much like home. Doesn't matter where I go next; it'll never be the same.
